problems.message: Dumps the whole circle-of-fifths document instead of answering "3 sharps: F# C# G#". The document says "5 (= C# major) | Cb major"; Cb major is enharmonic to B major (position 5), C# major is enharmonic to Db (position 7).

Triads are right; the voicings are not. Dm VexTab (1/6.1/5.3/4.2/3) = F Bb F A, not xx0231. "E dim 7-10-11-9-8-7" = B G C# E G B (C#m7b5/B); Edim is E G Bb. "Bb Barre at 1 (1-3-3-3-1-1)" = F C F Bb C F (Fsus4); Bb is x13331. F VexTab = F Bb F Bb C# F; Gm VexTab = G C G C D G (Gsus4); Am VexTab = A D A C# F. Only the C VexTab spells its chord.
Answers with the 7-note A natural minor (A B C D E F G); A minor pentatonic is A C D E G.
Describes only Aeolian (on C); no comparison. Dorian = 1 2 b3 4 5 6 b7: it differs from Aeolian only by the natural 6th.

Regex floor: no degree formula (1 2 b3 4 5 6 7, i.e. natural minor with raised 6th and 7th); the step pattern W-H-W-W-W-W-H is right. The "A melodic minor" tab plays D E F# A B C# E F# A B C# (no C, no G#: D major material, not A B C D E F# G#); it says it starts on the low E at fret 5 but starts on the A string; the VexTab is malformed.
Gives C Mixolydian (C D E F G A Bb); E Mixolydian is E F# G# A B C# D.
"raising the 7th a half-step (e.g., A -> A# in A natural minor)": the 7th of A minor is G, raised to G# (the answer itself then gives V = E-G#-B). The rest of the explanation is right.

"the 3rd and the 7th (e.g., B b in a G7)": G7 has B natural; the tritone is B-F. "the chord sits a half-step below the tonic's root ... (G -> Ab -> A -> C)": the root falls a fifth G -> C. Table "3rd (B) -> 3rd of I (E)": B rises to C. "7th (F) -> 5th of I (G) - down a step": F falls to E. "tritone (B-F) resolves to ... (E-G)": it resolves to C-E. G7 VexTab = G A E G C E (comment 320001 is right, but says low E muted); C VexTab = A F A B plus an invalid 1/0; "G7 shape at 3rd fret" VexTab is at fret 1 = F Bb F B C. Regex passed: new phrasing.

Theory is right (G7/Db7, shared B=Cb and F, Dm7-Db7-Cmaj7). "Full-root Db7 x45464" = Db G B F Ab: D string fret 5 is G, not a Db7 tone (Db7 = x46464). "Rootless drop-2 9-8-10-9 on A D G B" = F# Bb F Ab, not Db7; its claimed notes "Db, Ab, C, F" are Dbmaj7 (Db7 has Cb) and include the root of a "rootless" voicing.

V/V = D7 (D F# A C) is right. The "open D7" VexTab (0/4.2/3.1/2.0/1) = D A C E has no F#, the third; "String 1 2nd fret = E": high e fret 2 is F# (open D7 = xx0212). Also "V-to-V resolution" for V/V -> V.

"called Neapolitan-6: the interval between the bass and the soprano is a sixth": the 6 is the figured bass of first inversion. "bass ... to the dominant root (F -> E)" and "falls a whole step": in C the bass F rises a whole step to G. "Db -> C# -> D": bII falls a diminished third to the leading tone B (often via C over the cadential 6/4). "Ab -> B up a half step": Ab falls a half step to G (Ab-B is an augmented second).

It/Fr/Ger spellings in C (Ab C F#, Ab C D F#, Ab C Eb F#) and the outward resolution are right. French D called "b2": it is scale degree 2. Shapes: Italian 4-x-1-2-1-1 = Ab Eb A C F; French 4-3-1-2-1-1 = Ab C Eb A C F ("3rd-fret A string for the D": A3 is C); German 4-2-1-2-1-1 = Ab B Eb A C F ("2nd-fret A string (Eb)": A2 is B). "G7" 320003 = G B D G B G, a G triad. "top F# (1st-fret high e)": e fret 1 is F. The VexTabs disagree with the ASCII and are also wrong.

Chords are right (Cm7 x35343, F7 131211, Bbmaj7 x13231). Voice-leading tips are wrong: "C down a half-step to B (the b7 of F7)": the b7 of F7 is Eb, and C is a common tone. "G (D string 5 -> 1) drops a perfect fourth": G -> Eb is a major third. "F (5 of F7)": F is the root. "C (1st string 1)": e fret 1 is F. "Eb (b7) moves down to A": Eb falls to D, the 3rd of Bbmaj7. "Open-position F7" is a 1st-fret barre.

"a half cadence that begins on the tonic (I-V) is classified as an imperfect authentic cadence": an IAC ends on I; I-V is a half cadence. "the seventh resolves down a step (b7 -> 6)": the 7th of V7 is scale degree 4 and falls to 3. Plagal "soprano 2 -> 1" and "tenor stays on common tone 5": IV is 4-6-1, the common tone is 1. "bass moves stepwise from 4 to 1": 4 -> 1 is a fourth. I listed as a pre-dominant.

Leading tone "usually resolves downward ... B -> A": in V-vi it normally rises B -> C (doubled third of vi). "D -> C ... a half-step": whole step. "tritone (B-F) resolves to A-E": to C-E. D chord "x-0-2-3-2-0" = A E Bb C# E (D = xx0232). "3rd fret on the B string (B)": it is D. "Beethoven 5, 2nd movement (C minor)": that movement is in Ab major.

Prose is right (B up to C, F down to E). G7 VexTab (3/6.3/5.2/4.0/3) = G C E G, no B or F; its comment says A string fret 2 = A (B) and G string fret 1 = G (Ab). C VexTab (3/5.3/4.0/2) = C F B. "B (2nd string, 2nd fret) -> C (2nd string, open)": B string fret 2 is C# and open is B; the move is open B -> fret 1 C.
Voicing search with tags [the] returned ten Cadd9/D, Cadd9/E and Cadd9 shapes (labels correct, e.g. x-5-5-7-5-8 = D G D E C). It never answers: A-shape C barre = x-3-5-5-5-3 at the 3rd fret.
